headline: High: open-webui’s broad network/MCP/tooling can amplify cognee outputs into unsafe actions and data exposure, while shared-state conflicts and compliance gaps remain plausible.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: open-webui explicitly supports MCP, plugins, tools, and OpenAPI tool servers, so it can ingest external content and act on it; cognee produces documents, workflows, and decisions. The pair has a plausible instruction-hijack path if cognee output is fed into open-webui without sanitization. No direct shared-channel evidence is provided, so uncertainty keeps this at medium.
conditions: IF cognee outputs are pasted or routed into open-webui tool prompts without filtering, injection is possible.
IF open-webui MCP or plugin inputs are treated as instructions rather than data, attacker-controlled text can steer actions.
mitigations: Disable MCP/plugins for the session.
Paste only quoted excerpts, never raw instructions.
Add a fixed delimiter and instruction prefix when transferring text.
Review any tool call before execution.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between the agents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: cognee touches personal data, finance data, support history, and documents, while open-webui handles files, persistent memory, API keys, and can reach Google Drive/OneDrive/Search APIs. A shared workspace or mounted volume would let sensitive cognee data flow into open-webui’s broader egress surface. The profiles do not prove a shared workspace, so this is medium rather than high.
conditions: IF both agents access the same mounted volume or local files, sensitive data can be read by open-webui.
IF open-webui is configured to send file contents to external APIs, copied cognee data may leave the environment.
mitigations: Separate the agents onto different volumes.
Remove sensitive files from any shared directory.
Turn off external connectors for the transfer session.
Use a redaction pass before copying data.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent ACLs on shared storage.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: cognee has session memory and supports multiple instances, while open-webui uses persistent shared web-app sessions with Redis-backed multi-worker state and can spawn subprocesses. If both operate on the same mutable workspace or backend resource, concurrent writes and state races are plausible. The profiles do not show a shared target, so medium is the right uncertainty-aware choice.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory, database, or session store, state conflicts can occur.
IF open-webui workers and cognee instances share a mutable backend without locks, last-write-wins races are possible.
mitigations: Assign separate working directories.
Avoid concurrent writes during handoff.
Pause one agent before the other mutates shared state.
Snapshot the workspace before transfer.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: cognee emits decisions, workflows, and successful implementations, and open-webui is a tool-using web UI that can forward model outputs into plugins or external APIs. If open-webui treats cognee output as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream actions or rendered advice. Because open-webui has action-capable integrations by default, the blast radius is high.
conditions: IF open-webui forwards cognee-generated decisions into tools or APIs without verification, incorrect outputs can trigger actions.
IF cognee outputs are used as source-of-truth content in open-webui, downstream users may act on unverified claims.
mitigations: Require human review before any tool call.
Mark cognee output as untrusted text.
Disable auto-execution of plugins.
Add a verification step against source data.
requires-engineering: implement confidence-gated action policies.

E_compliance.rationale: cognee touches personal data, finance data, support history, and documents, while open-webui handles files, persistent memory, analytics, and external connectors. That creates a plausible retention and residency mismatch if the same regulated data is routed through open-webui’s broader storage and API surfaces. No explicit residency or certification data is provided, so the risk is medium, not high.
conditions: IF regulated customer data is routed through open-webui connectors, retention and transfer obligations may be triggered.
IF open-webui logs or persists the same data class longer than cognee, deletion/export obligations can diverge.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of open-webui.
Disable analytics and long-term memory.
Review retention settings before use.
Export and delete test records after validation.
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls.
